This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:

- #35294: Desktop startup blocked by a hanging `models.dev` fetch (same ESTABLISHED-but-idle TCP connection pattern during init, same lack of timeout)
- #35090: `models.dev` fetch lacks network resilience — no timeout, no backoff, causes startup stalls in restricted/flaky networks
- #9493: opencode quits/hangs when `models.dev` is not responding (earlier instance of the same root cause)

Your investigation (ESTABLISHED connection to `172.67.69.147` = `models.dev`, no progress, no error, no timeout) points to the same underlying issue described in those reports. The intermittency you observed — healthy windows vs. failure windows — is consistent with `models.dev` itself being slow or partially degraded rather than fully unreachable, which would explain why `curl` succeeds (fast path) while the opencode fetch stalls on a slower/different connection.

The second hang shape (no sockets at all) may be a separate code path, so it could be worth noting as an addition to one of those existing issues rather than a duplicate.
The comments contain the resolution. The issue was about "Upstream request failed" errors on Go models.

I also hope this feature can be added soon. I've been struggling with OpenCode's account management for a long time. After changing my primary GitHub email, when I logged back into OpenCode, I noticed my old email was still listed, and then my new email appeared as well. Every time I create a Key, two options show up—same Key but different emails. If I delete one, the other disappears too. This is a serious bug. I am experiencing the same issue on Windows, but it is not limited to Gradle or long-running commands.

I have intermittently seen the shell tool remain in the running state after apparently completed commands including:

* `.\gradlew.bat assembleDebug`, after either `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` or `BUILD FAILED`
* `git status`
* `git diff`
* `rg`
* PowerShell `Get-Content`

In each case, the expected output appears to be complete, but OpenCode does not continue to the next agent step until I manually interrupt it. Re-running the same command often completes normally, so the issue appears intermittent.

The short commands are especially notable because `git status`, `rg`, and ordinary `Get-Content` calls normally terminate immediately and do not leave persistent daemon processes.

Environment:

* OpenCode: `[VERSION]`
* OS: Windows 11 `[BUILD IF AVAILABLE]`
* Shell: PowerShell `[VERSION]`
* Terminal: `[WINDOWS TERMINAL / OTHER]`
* Installation method: `[NPM / BUN / SCOOP / OTHER]`

I saw that #29831 changes process completion from `close` to `exit`. I am reporting these additional command types because this may be broader than Gradle descendants retaining stdout/stderr handles. I can test the PR branch or provide debug logs and process-tree information if that would help.

Root cause of the opaque `Error: Unexpected error / ServeError` output here is tracked in #38738 — Effect's `ServeError` is a `Data.TaggedError` with an empty `message`, and opencode's `errorMessage()` never reads `.cause`, so the real `listen` errno is dropped.

Relevant to your mirrored-networking diagnosis: under Bun, `node:http` `listen()` reports **every** failure as `EADDRINUSE` (#38739) — verified against Node, which correctly returns `EADDRNOTAVAIL` / `EACCES` for the same binds. So the WSL sidecar failure may not be a port conflict at all; the errno cannot distinguish it. With #38738 applied the sidecar would print the actual cause instead of `ServeError`, which should settle it either way.

This issue might be a duplicate of or closely related to existing issues. Please check:
- #38739: Companion issue by the same author — covers Bun's errno collapsing (all listen failures reported as EADDRINUSE), which directly affects the fix proposed here
- #37718: Desktop WSL sidecar ServeError with mirrored networking — exhibits the same bare `ServeError` / `Unexpected error` output described here

Good catch on `movePath`, and your diagnosis is right.

It wouldn't have been fixed by #37679 either way, though. That PR targets `v2` and patches `packages/core/src/permission.ts`, while your failure goes through `packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts` on the v1 line. Different module, so it never reaches `apply_patch`.

Worth noting the nested shape doesn't exist on v2 at all. `apply_patch`'s successor there, `packages/core/src/tool/patch.ts`, passes no metadata and puts the file list in the typed `resources` field instead, so there's nothing left to strip below the top level. That's why the v2 fix is shallow.

The v1 bug is real and still on `dev`, though. `apply_patch.ts` sets `movePath: change.movePath` when building `metadata.files[]`, and that's undefined for every hunk that isn't a move, including adds and deletes.

To your question, yes, omit it at the construction site:

```ts
...(change.movePath ? { movePath: change.movePath } : {}),
```

Local, matches the optional type, and it keeps the change contained to the release line that has the bug.

Different branch and module, so this wants its own issue against `dev`. Happy to open it and credit your investigation.
